content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on **Creating Categorical Data**. Work through the listed subtopics (Specifying dtype="category", Creating Categorical objects, Defining permitted categories, Defining an ordered categorical type) as decisions in one small data workflow: identify the input and its labels, choose the relevant Pandas operation, then inspect the output shape, values, and types. Do not assume the result is correct solely because the code ran.

import pandas as pd

level = pd.Categorical(["high", "low", "medium"], categories=["low", "medium", "high"], ordered=True)
print((level[0] > level[1]))

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Avoid assuming inferred types are always correct, treating every repeated record as an error, or overlooking alignment by labels. Check the actual API documentation for the target version and assert the properties that matter to the task.
